headline: Scientists find air around a faraway planet

sources.title: Potential Atmosphere Detected on Habitable-Zone Exoplanet LHS 1140b
Astronomers spot first atmosphere around a potentially habitable alien world
Rocky Planet 48 Light-Years Away May Be First in a Habitable Zone With a Confirmed Atmosphere

chunks.text: For the first time ever, scientists have {{picked up}} signs of air around a small, rocky planet far from Earth. The planet, called LHS 1140 b, sits about 48 light-years away, in the area where the temperature could be just right for water. Finding air around such a planet is [[a huge deal]], because a planet needs air to {{hold on to}} heat and to protect any life. But the discovery soon {{turned into}} a real [[mystery]], with a strange [[twist]] no one expected.

chunks.text: LHS 1140 b is a super-Earth, which means it is rocky like Earth but much bigger. To study it, a team from Harvard University {{set out}} to watch the planet with a powerful telescope in Chile. In 2024, the telescope {{came across}} helium gas leaking from the top of the planet's air. Because the star {{gives off}} strong radiation, it slowly {{strips away}} this gas. It was a rare [[privilege]] to [[witness]] such a discovery.

chunks.text: Here is where things get strange. When the same team {{went back}} to check their work in 2025, the helium signal had completely disappeared. This is where the real puzzle {{comes in}}. Scientists think the planet's air may [[shift]] and change in ways we can actually see. Still, they are not [[certain]] yet, and more work is needed to {{figure out}} what is really {{going on}}.

chunks.text: To clear things up, the team will soon {{carry out}} new studies with the James Webb Space Telescope. Their main goal is to {{track down}} water, which would [[prove]] the air is real. If they {{pull off}} this hard task and [[succeed]], LHS 1140 b could become one of the best places to search for life beyond Earth. And that brings us a little closer to a question people have asked for thousands of years: are we alone?

tf.s: Scientists picked up signs of air around the rocky planet LHS 1140 b.
